en: Where are you going after class today?
I am meeting a friend downtown.
Are you watching a movie together with your friend?
Yes, we are watching an interesting movie at the cinema.

bg-d-01-01.q: Where is the second speaker meeting their friend?
bg-d-01-01.why: The second speaker answers '시내에서 친구를 만나요' (I am meeting a friend downtown).

bg-d-01-01.q: What will the two friends do together?
bg-d-01-01.why: They say '극장에서 재미있는 영화를 봐요' (We are watching an interesting movie at the cinema).
만나다 has the bright vowel ㅏ, conjugating to 만나요.

bg-d-01-01.q: Your friend asks: “오늘 수업 끝나고 어디 가요?” Reply that you are going to the cinema using 극장에 and 가요.
bg-d-01-01.why: 가다 ends in the stem vowel ㅏ, attaching -아요 to contract into 가요.

items: Conjugate verb stems ending in bright vowels ㅏ and ㅗ with -아요
Describe where you go and who you meet after class

en: It is lunchtime, let's eat together.
Sounds great, let's eat kimbap at the restaurant.
Do you read books at the library after eating?
Yes, I read Korean books at the library.

bg-d-01-02.q: What do the speakers plan to eat for lunch?
bg-d-01-02.why: The second speaker says '식당에서 김밥을 먹어요' (Let's eat kimbap at the restaurant).

bg-d-01-02.q: What will the second speaker study at the library?
bg-d-01-02.why: The speaker says '도서관에서 한국어를 배워요' (I learn Korean at the library).

bg-d-01-02.hint: I eat kimbap at the restaurant.
bg-d-01-02.why: 먹다 has the stem vowel ㅓ, so it attaches -어요 → 먹어요.

bg-d-01-02.q: Your friend asks what you do at the library. Reply that you read books using 책을 and 읽어요.
bg-d-01-02.why: 읽다 has the vowel ㅣ, which takes -어요 to form 읽어요.

items: Apply -어요 to verb stems ending in vowels other than ㅏ or ㅗ
Talk about everyday lunchtime routines and studying at the library

en: What are you drinking at the cafe right now?
Are you also writing a letter to give to your friend?
Yes, I am writing a congratulatory letter in Korean.

bg-d-01-03.q: What is the speaker drinking at the cafe?
bg-d-01-03.why: The second speaker answers '따뜻한 차를 마셔요' (I am drinking warm tea).
The text says '한국어로 축하 편지를 써요' (I am writing a congratulatory letter in Korean).
마시- + -어요 contracts ㅣ + 어 into 여 → 마셔요.

bg-d-01-03.q: Your friend asks what you do in the morning. Reply that you drink coffee using 커피를 and 마셔요.
bg-d-01-03.why: 마시다 contracts with -어요 to become 마셔요.

items: Fluently contract vowels without final consonants (ㅗ+아→와, ㅣ+어→여, ㅜ+어→워)
Order drinks and describe writing activities in Korean

en: The room is a bit warm, shall I open the window?
Yes, since the breeze is cool, let's open the window.
Where do you usually rest on weekends?
I rest well at home and exercise in the park.

bg-d-01-04.q: Why do the speakers open the window?
options: The room is warm and the breeze is cool
bg-d-01-04.why: The first speaker says '방이 좀 더운데 창문 열어요?' and the second agrees the breeze is cool.

bg-d-01-04.q: What does the second speaker do on weekends?
options: Rest at home and exercise in the park
bg-d-01-04.why: The speaker explains '집에서 푹 쉬고 공원에서 운동해요' (I rest well at home and exercise in the park).

bg-d-01-04.hint: Since it is cool, let's open the window.
bg-d-01-04.why: 열다 has vowel ㅓ, taking -어요 to become 열어요.

bg-d-01-04.q: Your friend asks where you rest on weekends. Reply that you rest at home using 집에서 and 쉬어요.
bg-d-01-04.why: 쉬다 ends in vowel ㅟ, which is not ㅏ or ㅗ, so it takes -어요 → 쉬어요.

items: Accurately differentiate confusing verb stems (살다 vs 열다, 닫다 vs 쉬다)
Confidently produce appropriate polite forms in natural conversational context
